findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext discards all recorded log state
findings.body: FromContext returns a brand-new TestLogger instead of the receiver (or a logger sharing the receiver's state). LoggerMiddleware now logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), so any test that injects a TestLogger and then asserts on InfoLogs/DebugLogs/etc. of the injected instance will observe zero calls because the log was recorded on the discarded new instance. This makes the fake unable to verify the new LoggerMiddleware path and can silently turn existing assertions vacuous or failing.

findings.title: "Plugin Request Completed" log line loses traceID field
findings.body: The old logRequest explicitly added traceID (via tracing.TraceIDFromContext) plus pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname as log parameters. The new version relies solely on m.logger.FromContext(ctx). The ContextualLoggerMiddleware only sets endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID and uname via log.WithContextualAttributes; it never adds a traceID, and neither does grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext. Consequently the completed-request log no longer carries traceID, breaking correlation between this log line and traces that dashboards/alerts/log queries may rely on.

findings.title: Adding FromContext to Logger interface breaks other implementations
findings.body: Logger is an interface; adding the FromContext(context.Context) Logger method is a breaking change for every implementation outside the two updated in this PR (pkg/plugins/log/logger.go and fake.go), including mocks/fakes in other packages or downstream consumers. Such implementations will no longer satisfy plog.Logger and will fail to compile until updated. The PR should update/search for all in-repo implementations and call out the break, or avoid widening the interface (e.g. optional interface checked by type assertion in LoggerMiddleware).

findings.title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware has no test coverage
findings.body: This new middleware is now solely responsible for putting endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname into the request context, and LoggerMiddleware depends on it to produce those fields. No test file for contextual_logger_middleware.go is added, and the renamed metrics_middleware_test.go (still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware) does not assert contextual attributes. A regression in instrumentContext (wrong keys, missing datasource/user fields, or reordering in CreateMiddlewares so LoggerMiddleware runs before it) would silently drop those fields from all plugin request logs without any test failing.
